source.title: Geometric Dynamics of Signal Propagation Predict Trainability of Transformers
source.authors: Aditya Cowsik; Tamra Nebabu; Xiaoliang Qi; Surya Ganguli

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how initialization hyperparameters and signal-propagation properties relate to final test loss by training randomly initialized transformers on Food-101; this is a different architecture, dataset, and outcome measure from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's separately reported training results on Food-101 test loss. The theoretical and numerical signal-propagation results and their parameter sweeps do not report training classification error and are not rows for the listed versions. Values in Figure 7 are figure-only; the text describes the trends but gives no precise plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization signal propagation and final test loss in a residual transformer. It does not measure the plain-network learning speed or trainable depth named in V4, or the outcomes named in the other versions. Its related results therefore fit no listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' empirical conclusion: in the tested Food-101 transformer sweep, jointly near-zero angle and gradient exponents predict low final test loss, whereas either condition alone is insufficient. The authors describe the joint conditions as necessary and sufficient; this is an interpretation of the fixed-depth, fixed-duration experiment and fitted loss relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly initialized transformer trained on Food-101 with Adam; measures final test loss rather than training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks. The experiment sweeps residual-branch and MLP-weight initialization parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Final test loss varies with the initial angle and gradient exponents, which vary with α and σw. The text reports high-loss points even where either individual exponent is zero; both constraints together predict low loss.

fits_no_version.finding: For a 16-layer tanh transformer trained on Food-101 for 15 epochs, low final test loss occurs near jointly zero angle and gradient exponents. Either exponent near zero alone can coexist with high test loss. A fitted combination of both exponents predicts final test loss across the initialization sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization signal-propagation exponents jointly predict final test loss in the tested residual vision transformer.

record.problems: Training results are presented as plots without precise numerical values in the text; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported for the training sweep. The outcome is test loss, not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying training-outcome rows are stated in text. Figures 2–6 show signal propagation and exponent calculations, not training classification error or final training loss, so they are not included.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, plain networks, or Fixup.
Initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and maximum trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, training-loss recovery, curvature changes, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The signal-propagation experiments, including causal-attention results, concern initialization dynamics rather than measured learning speed or trainable depth. They do not supply additional qualifying results for V4.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, including corrupted or random labels; comparison with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks as depth increases; effects of shortcuts, special initialization, and normalization on classification training error.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for plain networks, including trainability speed and maximum trainable depth.
Training behavior above or near stability limits, loss transients, curvature, and sharpness.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed, accuracy, or learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: 16-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam while sweeping α and σw; test loss measured after training.
rows.note: The authors state that the minimum achievable test loss increases with distance from either λg = 0 or λa = 0, and that jointly small departures predict low test loss. No precise per-setting values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The setup and qualitative test-loss trends are correctly recorded, but final test loss after 15 epochs cannot establish any listed version. Figure 7 gives uniform guessing as a reference loss, ln(101) ≈ 4.6; the record omits this reference. Qualitative trends are readable even though precise per-setting values are unavailable.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
